public_payload.normalized_proposition: Users will eventually be limited to token use matching their subscription price, lowering product value and subscriber numbers.

statement.excerpt: At some point, users will be forced to burn tokens at a rate that actually matches their subscription costs, which will reduce the value of the product, which will in turn reduce the amount of subscribers they will have.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: tokens at a rate that actually matches their subscription costs
reduce the value of the product
in turn reduce the amount of subscribers
our_interpretation: The surrounding text identifies Anthropic and OpenAI subscription services.

The ordinary reading is that the providers stop subsidizing included token use by imposing cost-covering allowances, reducing usable service for the subscription price and causing paid subscriber counts to fall.
The wording also permits comparison with retail API prices. Those prices must not be assumed to equal the providers' delivery costs.
Subscriber decline means a reduction in paid subscriber numbers, not merely complaints, cancellations by some customers, or slower growth.
The successive effects are parts of the forecast, not an independently stated conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Both providers impose usage allowances that approximately align delivery costs with subscription receipts, reducing comparable product value and causing paid subscriber counts to decline.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishing that a claimed cost-parity adjustment did not reduce value or cause subscriber losses would reject that episode as fulfillment. A finite period without such an adjustment cannot refute the indefinite forecast.
